title: The Single Easiest Way To Build Rapport
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin makes the case for the end-of-class fist bump as an unusually simple, high-leverage rapport-building habit. He explains its mechanisms: it 'cleans the slate,' signaling that whatever tension occurred during class carries no grudge into the next encounter; it requires a small act of reciprocation from the student, an implicit buy-in to the relationship; it includes eye contact and a smile, which research-adjacent claims say lowers cortisol and increases serotonin, reinforcing connection; and it guarantees a brief, personal touchpoint with every student daily, including quiet students who might otherwise go unnoticed. He notes the gesture can feel awkward at first but becomes natural over time, eventually spreading among students themselves, and gives a practical tip on execution — a light tap near the wrist rather than a hard knuckle punch — closing with a simple daily instruction to just do it at the door every day.
points: The end-of-class fist bump is presented as the single easiest and most effective way to build rapport.
It 'cleans the slate,' signaling no grudges are carried from classroom tension into the next interaction.
It requires a small reciprocal act from the student — an implicit buy-in to the relationship.
It guarantees a brief daily touchpoint with every student, including quiet students who might otherwise be overlooked.
The gesture, awkward at first, becomes natural over time and often spreads to students fist-bumping each other.
quotes: The lowly fist bump, offered as students file out of your classroom, is arguably the easiest way to build rapport.
No matter what happens during class, no matter how strongly you challenge your students or raise your standards, the end-of-day fist bump says that it’s all in the past.
Although offered and never forced, a fist bump requires students to reach out toward you. It’s an act of faith and reciprocation.
The end-of-period fist bump ensures that you make a quick check-in with every student every day.
A simple tap of the knuckles, like all touch, decreases cortisol and increases serotonin. It relaxes the central nervous system and makes us feel good.
Every day, as soon as the dismissal bell rings, stand at your door, smile, make eye contact, and offer your fist to every student.
